title: Residue exactness of finite free complexes is universally tensor exact in one degree
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $P^\bullet$ a cochain complex of $R$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with every $P^j$ finite free [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Fix an integer $i$. Assume $H^i(P^\bullet\otimes_R R/\mathfrak m)=0$ for every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $R$, where tensor is ordinary termwise tensor [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Then $H^i(P^\bullet\otimes_R M)=0$ for every $R$-module $M$. No boundedness or flatness hypothesis on $M$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 068U, lemma-cut-complex-in-two, direct matrix proof; Tag 068V, lemma-check-perfect-pointwise, implication (3) to (1)

proof.text: For every maximal ideal m, restrict ordinary extension of scalars back to R and use ModuleCat.extendScalarsCompRestrictScalarsIso to identify its cochain complex with termwise tensor by R/m. The exact faithful restriction functor detects exactness. Regard R/m as a field, and tensor the exact short complex with Frac(R/m), which is a free and hence flat R/m-module. Reassociate scalar extension using ModuleCat.extendScalarsComp. This gives precisely the residue hypothesis of the cancellation theorem. All comparisons are explicit natural isomorphisms mapped to complexes.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-free-complex-residue-degree-cancellation] at degree i and each maximal m. Obtain f outside m and a homotopy equivalence between P_f and Q with Q.X i zero. The strong monoidal scalar-extension functor gives the explicit cochain isomorphism (P tensor M)_f isomorphic to P_f tensor M_f (Functor.Monoidal.commTensorRight). Map the homotopy equivalence by tensorRight M_f and apply HomotopyEquiv.toHomologyIso. The tensor of the zero middle object is zero, so (P tensor M)_f is exact at i. This is valid for every M, without flatness.

Let s be the set of f for which (P tensor M)_f is exact at i. Its span is top: otherwise [lem-weil-pbc-proper-ideal-contained-in-maximal] gives a maximal m containing the span, but the f constructed for that m belongs to s and is outside m. This contradiction also handles the zero ring without choosing a maximal ideal.

Apply the proved Mathlib exact_of_isLocalized_span to the three linear maps of (P tensor M).sc i. For each f in s use the concrete localization module R_f tensor N and map x to 1 tensor x. IsLocalization.tensorProduct_isLocalizedModule supplies its universal property. IsLocalizedModule.linearMap_ext and map_apply identify the localized differential with tensorLeft R_f of the differential. Restrict scalar extension and use the explicit identity linear isomorphism from its induced scalar action to the canonical localization action; the symmetry of tensor identifies it with tensorLeft R_f. Local exactness therefore gives global exactness. Finally ExactAt.isZero_homology proves the conclusion. These are already proved generic Mathlib tools; no new unproved localization fact is used.

lean.statement:
theorem isZero_homology_tensor_of_residue
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (P : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ)
    (hfree : ∀ j : ℤ, Module.Free R (P.X j))
    (hfinite : ∀ j : ℤ, Module.Finite R (P.X j)) (i : ℤ)
    (hresidue : ∀ (m : Ideal R), m.IsMaximal → IsZero
      ((((tensorRight (ModuleCat.of R (R ⧸ m))).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P).homology
        i)) (M : ModuleCat.{u} R) :
    IsZero ((((tensorRight M).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P).homology i)
